item.title: Runnin' Rebels improve to 2-0 with gutsy win over Samford
item.description: UNLV forward Tyrin Jones (6) looks over NAU guard Ryan Ableman (11) during first half of college basketball game against NAU on Tuesday November 3, 2026 at Thomas & Mack Center in Las Vegas. LAS VEGAS – Runnin’ Rebels head coach Josh Pastner says that his team’s biggest strength is that their go-to man is the open man. That claim rang true in UNLV’s 88-79 victory over Samford at Thomas & Mack Center on Saturday. Five Rebels scored in double figures as UNLV improved to 2-0 — underpinning their selfless mindset to start the campaign. Sophomore Cam Miles led the way this time with 20 points — shooting 4-for-9 from three-point range and 8-for-8 from the free-throw line. Tyrin Jones made winning plays in bunches, chipping in 17 points, five rebounds, six blocks, and two steals. He drew praise from Pastner for knocking down seven of his 10 attempts at the charity stripe. Elsewhere, last game’s hero Sebastian Mack poured in 17 points on 7-for-13 shooting. He didn’t have to erupt today because this Rebels team is constructed to play together. It just so happened to be Miles’ turn to set a new scoring career high. “I have to give it all to my teammates,” Miles said afterward. “As soon as I came in, they welcomed me in as a brother. The chemistry that we have is amazing. They give me confidence and energy. They’re always talking to me, making sure I’m up.” Miles oozed confidence as he buried a 28-foot triple with 1:25 remaining in the second half, all but putting the visitors away at 88-78. Jones made his presence felt on both ends of the floor as the Rebels struggled to find separation from the pesky Bulldogs, who hung around tough. UNLV finally created some daylight between the two teams late. Jones grabbed an offensive board and kicked the ball out to Miles for a three-pointer before converting a couple of free throws and finishing strong at the basket on the following play with the shot clock dwindling. That made it 85-78 — tying the hosts’ largest lead of the game — with 3:06 left to play. Pastner was in great spirits entering the media room postgame. He’s pleased with the work his team has put in their first two games. “I think both teams we played this week are good teams,” he said. “There is so much parity amongst college basketball now.” Pastner shared that his three keys to the victory were: adhering to the game plan by guarding the three-point line — with Samford being a shooting team, free throws, and offensive rebounding. The Rebels held the visitors to just 5-for-20 from beyond the arc. 20 of the Bulldogs’ 62 field goal attempts came from deep, when usually they take about half of their shots from the outside, according to Pastner. UNLV made 25 of 32 free throws, limiting Samford to just 19 attempts (14 makes) with disciplined defense. The hosts out-rebounded the Bulldogs 38-28, with the 11 offensive boards providing a decisive edge. The Rebels are feeling really good about their start to the year. item.title: Kansas football vs UCF grades: KU’s report card from Big 12 matchup
item.description: LAWRENCE — Kansas football suffered a 33-32 loss on Saturday, Nov. 7 at home in a Big 12 Conference matchup against UCF. Here’s how the Jayhawks (3-6, 1-5 in Big 12) graded out in their defeat against the Knights (5-4, 3-3): Offense: Kansas finds its form in 2nd half, but early struggles linger Kansas put together just one scoring drive in the first half, and that touchdown came on a drive that needed four plays to go 3 yards. But while the Jayhawks were much improved in the second half, as sophomore quarterback Isaiah Marshall thrived, that effort came up short. It took them too long to get going, and that, along with a turnover in each half, helped sink KU’s chances at a victory. Grade: C RELATED: Kansas football vs UCF final score, highlights from Big 12 matchup Defense: Kansas fails to get decisive final stop All Kansas needed to do with little time remaining in the second half was get one more stop, but the Jayhawks weren’t able to do that. Instead, they watched UCF drive for the go-ahead score with barely any time left in the fourth quarter. There was a lot to like, such as four sacks, 11 tackles for loss and a pair of turnovers. But at game’s end, the Knights still finished with 33 points. Grade: C- Special teams: Kansas has some success, but not enough KU redshirt sophomore kicker Martin Connington did hit his lone field goal and all his extra points, but the Jayhawks didn’t see a lot of success elsewhere. Kansas allowed too much on kick returns, and didn’t do much itself when it had chances on returns. KU freshman punter Matt Gill did have a punt land inside the 20-yard line, but could have performed better overall. Grade: B- Coaching: KU battles back, falls short When UCF took a 26-7 in the third quarter, it looked like Kansas was on its way to being blown out in front of the Jayhawks’ home crowd. But while KU would go on to score 25 points unanswered and give fans a reason to believe, it wasn't able to complete the victory. It’s yet another close loss for this Kansas program under coach Lance Leipold. Grade: C- Overall grade: C- Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. item.description: OBETZ — The fourth time is a charm for Shelby’s Anna Will. After qualifying for the state cross country championships in each of the last three seasons, but coming up short in her quest for an All-Ohio honor, the senior accomplished the elusive goal when she finished 33 rd with a 19:29.2 to take second team All-Ohio honors. LEXINGTON TAKES STATE RUNNER-UP HONORS: Lexington's amazing journey leads to Division II state runner-up finish “I am really happy about it,” Will said. “Every year, I have come here with the goal of earning All-Ohio and I have never got it. Finally getting it my senior year and my last race in a Shelby jersey is thrilling and means so much to me. It is something I have been working for since I was a freshman.” Last week at the regional meet, Will got boxed in and while she still earned an individual qualifying spot, she felt like she was held back from running her absolute best. So, she changed her strategy at Saturday’s Ohio High School Athletic Association State Cross Country Championships and sprinted off of the line to get ahead of the pack. It worked well for her as she built a big enough advantage to withstand some late kicks from fellow runners to secure an All-Ohio spot. “It was definitely a tough race because you pretty much have to sprint right out of the gate,” Will said. “I am the kind of racer who would rather get out in a good spot and fall back a little bit rather than sit back and try to move up later. Knowing I had to go out faster was the right move because it put me in a better spot.” As a freshman, Will was 71 st with a 20:07.3 before taking 48 th with a 19:10.39 as a sophomore and 59 th with a 19:32.04 last season. She finally broke through as a senior and will join the All-Ohio honors at Shelby High School. “It is all thanks to my teammates and coaches,” Will said. “I would not be here without their support and encouragement. item.title: Russell vents fury at Mercedes after missing out on pole in São Paulo
item.description: FILE PHOTO - British formula One driver George Russell of team Mercedes speaks to the media at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, ahead of the Mexican Formula One Grand Prix. (is associated with: «Russell vents fury at Mercedes after missing out on pole in São Paulo») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa George Russell was again left furious with his Mercedes team after being pipped to pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris. Norris, deposed as world champion by Kimi Antonelli last weekend, conquered thunderstorms to clinch an impressive pole as the rain poured down. Russell was facing a five-place grid penalty due to an engine change but was still determined to land pole as he and Norris slugged it out. But he was told to back off on his final flying lap before the rain worsened and his chance had gone. "You told me to back off, what the hell?" Russell bellowed on the radio. Team principal Toto Wolff tried to calm his driver by saying: "George, you are p2." That seemed to make matters worse, as Russell barked: "P2? I don't want to be P2, I want to be P1!" It adds to a season of frustration for pre-season title favourite Russell, having had to watch 20-year-old team-mate Antonelli storm to the title while he says he had been undone by issues in 14 of the 20 weekends prior to this. "Congrats to Lando but that was a pole lap and a misjudgement on our side," Russell said. "For me personally, given the circumstances of last week, it would have meant a lot to me to take pole today. "I missed it last week by nine milliseconds, but that was a real surprise. Today I really felt every lap I was doing was... I was at the top of the leaderboard most laps I completed. "So yeah, I'm really disappointed with how that panned out. In the scheme of things, it doesn't change a huge amount." Russell was asked about the message from Wolff but played down any frustration over it. "When you're a driver, you're the one who feels it the most," he added. "You've got to remember, we collectively made a misjudgement today. And there's members of my team who are going to be feeling as bad as I am currently. So it's important to remember that and we need to just keep the morale high. "There's no point for pole, but it would have just been a nice little one to add to the tally." Wolff admitted in a video posted by Mercedes they may have made the wrong call with Russell behind Alex Albon on track, saying: "George was absolutely the quickest and should have been on pole. We are trying to do our best, I'm not sure we should have aborted the lap." Russell will start seventh, one of a number of drivers hit by grid drops. Lewis Hamilton received a 10-place penalty but his new engine began smoking during practice and Ferrari ultimately had to change his entire power unit. He will start from the back alongside Max Verstappen, while Charles Leclerc starts 14th after his 10-place drop. item.title: Grêmio are the first finalists of the 2026 Copa do Brasil
item.description: Grêmio are the first finalists of the 2026 Copa do Brasil Grêmio are the first finalists of the 2026 Copa do Brasil Credits: LUCAS UEBEL/GREMIO FBPA Grêmio drew 1–1 with Atlético-MG this Saturday (7) at Arena MRV in Belo Horizonte to reach the 2026 Copa do Brasil final. Having won the first leg 2–0 in Porto Alegre, the result in the Minas Gerais capital was enough to secure the team from Rio Grande do Sul a place in the final. Atlético-MG, who needed to win by at least two goals to force a penalty shootout, pressed from the start and opened the scoring with a stunning long-range strike from left-back Renan Lodi in the 26th minute. Around ten minutes later, striker Carlos Vinicius equalized for Grêmio, who also benefited from an excellent performance by goalkeeper Weverton. Grêmio will contest the Copa do Brasil final for the tenth time in their history and await the outcome of the tie between Vasco and Palmeiras, who meet this Sunday (8) at 5 p.m. (Brasília time) at São Januário in Rio. Palmeiras hold a 1–0 lead. Whether they face Vasco or Palmeiras, the team from Rio Grande do Sul will be seeking their sixth title in the competition, which would put them level with Cruzeiro as the most successful club in Copa do Brasil history. They currently have five titles: 1989, 1994, 1997, 2001 and 2016. Reaching the final guarantees Grêmio at least a place in the preliminary rounds of the 2027 CONMEBOL Libertadores, the berth awarded to the runners-up. The champions will qualify for the group stage of the 2027 CONMEBOL Libertadores. item.title: Dominant wins for Corning, Horseheads, TAE, Waverly in football semis
item.description: Corning, Horseheads, Waverly, and Thomas A. Edison were dominant in Section 4 football semifinal contests, earning spots in championship games next week. Watkins Glen/Odessa-Montour fell short against defending state champion Tioga Central in a Class D semifinal. A recap of Elmira-Corning region teams in sectional semifinals played Friday, Nov. 6 and Saturday, Nov. 7. Class AA: Corning 43, Ithaca 14 Hours after it was announced he was named the section's Class AA Player of the Year by the Section 4 Football Coaches Association , Corning's John Graham returned the opening kickoff 85 yards for a touchdown to set the tone in the Hawks' home semifinal triumph Friday night. "When we're clicking on all three sides of the ball, we're pretty good and we're tough to beat," Corning head coach Mike Johnston Jr. said. "To open the game up with the kickoff return was huge. He shows why he's the Section 4 Class AA Player of the Year and continues to make big plays for us." Graham added touchdown runs of 5 yards and 1 yard as Corning led 30-7 at halftime on the way to its second lopsided win this season against the Little Red. Corning, which began its combined program in 2010, has never lost to Ithaca. Graham finished with 96 yards on 13 rushes on a night Corning had 10 players run the ball. Fellow wingback Keegan Kelly added 86 yards on eight rushes to go with an interception on defense. Fullback Keegan VanCise carried 14 times for 78 yards, including a 1-yard touchdown. Ashton Neally added two touchdowns for the Hawks, the first on a 19-yard reception of a Nate Bretch throw, and the second on a 4-yard run that put Corning up, 44-7, just over two minutes into the final quarter. "It wasn't like somebody ran for 200 yards," Johnston said. "It was a collective effort by our team. A lot of the credit goes to our line. We were able to throw the ball tonight as well, and our defense was pretty solid as well. Just an all-around great effort by everybody." Touchdowns for Ithaca (5-5) came on a 36-yard run from Jasmir Robbins in the first half, and a 29-yard strike from Leo Fiorello to Shy'von Williams late in the game. Robbins rushed for 72 yards on eight carries. He sat out the second half after he was shaken up on the final play of the first half. Corning responded after a 33-7 loss to Union-Endicott in last week's regular-season finale. Little went right for the Hawks in that game, including more than 200 penalty yards, a dropped touchdown, and some injuries that sidelined key players in the second half. "I'd like to think that we turned the corner," Johnston said. "We've still got a ways to go with some guys, getting them healthy. I know Elmira gets the bye week and their kids will be back to full go." Up next : Corning (6-4) will play Elmira (6-3) in the championship game at 6 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 at Elmira's Thomas J. Hurley Athletic Complex. Elmira topped Corning, 14-8, in the regular season and has beaten the Hawks in the last three Section 4 Class AA finals.

item.title: Bill Belichick reacts to Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots honor
item.description: EAST HARTFORD, Conn. — After his North Carolina team finished off its win at UConn in his first game back in New England, former Patriots coach Bill Belichick responded to events happening in Foxborough. About 100 miles away at Gillette Stadium, Rob Gronkowski was being inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame. During his press conference Friday, Gronkowski praised Belichick and his contributions to the tight end’s development . “He played a tremendous role in who I am as a player. I really loved the way he challenged me,” Gronkowski said. “He’s the best football coach I’ve ever seen in my life, that I’ve ever been a part of as well. ... I thank him for that and I wouldn’t be here without him.” Belichick, who won six Super Bowls in New England, has often steered clear of any Patriots-related discussion after being fired by the team. But he made an exception for Gronkowski. Belichick smiled when told what Gronkowski said. He revealed that he’d reached out to his former star to congratulate him. “That’s nice of Rob to say that,” he said during his postgame press conference. “I talked to Rob and congratulated him on his selection into the Patriots Hall of Fame. Well deserved. He was the best tight end in football during his time and one of the best of all time. I’m proud of Rob and what he’s accomplished. “He came a long, long way from barely playing in college at Arizona,” Belichick continued, “to where he ended up, which was an incredible credit to him, his work ethic, his toughness and his dependability. It’s a hard position to play, but he excelled at it. We wouldn’t have won as many games as we did without him, I can tell you that. He’s a big part of it. item.title: Billam-Smith stopped as Clarke repeats amateur win
item.description: Chev Clarke (left) had previously beaten Chris Billam-Smith in a three-round amateur contest [Getty Images] Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight on Saturday. Londoner Clarke landed a big right hand at the start of the seventh round and although Billam-Smith beat the count, he was down again moments later after a barrage of punches. The contest was allowed to continue but the Bournemouth fighter looked unsteady on his legs and when Clarke connected with two more blows, the referee stepped in. Billam-Smith immediately protested against the decision, while Clarke stood in the middle of the ring shrugging his shoulders. Clarke moves to 13 wins with two defeats and inflicts the third professional defeat for Billam-Smith who also lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019. "I do what champions do," said Clarke, who also beat Billam-Smith when they met in the amateur ranks a decade ago. "I'm happy. Arsenal won and I won. My training camp was good and you saw that in the ring. I'll take all-comers going forward." The likes of heavyweight Johnny Fisher, Traitors star King Kenny and strongman Eddie Hall were all spotted watching on from ringside in a Copper Box arena that was far from full, with just the lower tier of seats open for fans. After a slow start to the contest with lots of holding, Clarke looked the sharper man as he landed some clean shots on the former world champion. In the second round, the Londoner landed a big overhand right to the side of Billam-Smith's head. Clarke also connected in the third round with a big uppercut and an overhand right that snapped back Billam-Smith's head. The former world champion, struggling to find his rhythm, was caught by another uppercut before Billam-Smith responded with a short right hook that made Clarke stumble back to his corner. But in the seventh round Clarke broke Billam-Smith down, scoring two quick knockdowns before the referee intervened. Fight promoter Dana White said after the fight that he felt the decision to stop the fight might have been a little premature. item.description: Credit: BTN A little over two weeks ago, Mike Locksley stood on the Maryland Terrapins’ sidelines as their head football coach. On Saturday, he sat in the Big Ten Network studio watching them snap a 13-game Big Ten losing streak against the Purdue Boilermakers. The Terps held on to defeat the Boilermakers 34-29 in West Lafayette, Indiana, and afterward interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim received a Gatorade bath and was carried off the field, creating a heartwarming scene. That scene got a little awkward when BTN left the game and returned to its studio show, where Locksley, fired Oct. 21 after eight seasons , was asked to comment on the victory and celebration. The former coach was graceful, praising the team and Aazaar, and noting that he’d picked them to win the game beforehand. “Congrats to Coach Aazaar and the Maryland Terrapin football team. It was a complimentary game,” he said. “When you look in the first half, the way the defense did a great job of holding them to field goals, and then the offense comes out, four TDs in four straight drives to blow the game open and then win it at the end in a close game at the end.” Fellow BTN analyst Gerry DiNardo seemed to understand the uncomfortable nature of the moment, and took a moment to point out that quarterback Malik Washington, who passed for 253 yards and was responsible for four touchdowns, was Locksley’s recruit. “Malik Washington’s not at Maryland if it wasn’t for you,” said DiNardo, patting his fellow analyst’s arm. “I appreciate that,” replied Locksley. item.title: 5 major takeaways from Penn State’s nail-biting win over Washington
item.description: It feels like Penn State has finally regained control over its season. After a four-game losing streak that followed a 3-0 start to the season, the blue and white have won two in a row, and it looks like they truly belong in the Big Ten. The Nittany Lions took on Washington on Saturday afternoon, and they won 28-25 in what was almost a mirror image of the Wisconsin game earlier in the season. The offense moved the ball and scored at will in the first half, while the defense put a familiar beatdown on the Huskies ’ offense. But then the offense went cold in the final two quarters, and the defense softened up and allowed the Huskies back in the game. However, Penn State was able to salt away the game in the end, and it escaped Washington with a win. Here are five of the biggest takeaways from the team’s second conference win of the season. We belong For a while there, it looked like head coach Matt Campbell and his gang of Iowa State transfers were no match for the Big Ten. They lost their first four games in the conference, and they were getting out-coached and outplayed for much of that time. But after back-to-back wins, with those Cyclones players being the focal points, their viability in the conference is no longer in question. There may not be much to accomplish for the team this season, but this is solid groundwork for the development of the program going forward. Beggars can’t be choosers Washington might not be the cream of the crop in the Big Ten, but they are certainly a good team. Penn State’s fans have been starving for a win against a team that has some life, and they finally got it this week. If may not have been the prettiest game, and the Nittany Lions may have avoided a catastrophe at the end of the game, but a win is a win. A victory was what everyone wanted, so we can’t complain about the path it took to get here. Competition It looked like Koby Howard was Penn State’s clear-cut best wide receiver when the season began. Now that he’s been out of action for more than two months, we’re finding out that it may not be the case. Wide receiver Chase Sowell has thrived in Howard’s absence, and he had the best game of his career by far on Saturday. He finished the contest with four catches for 125 yards and a touchdown, and he had a number of highlight plays that made him look like a star. Not only is it looking like the Nittany Lions have two No. 1 receivers, but they might both be stars as well. Rookie wall Linebacker Josiah Zayas struggled mightily for the first time all season. The true freshman got juked out on the very first play from scrimmage, and it set the table for the rest of the game. The Huskies tried to make a late push, and on the touchdown they scored to make the game 28-17, Zayas seemed confused about what he was supposed to be doing in coverage. He then gave up another touchdown on a fourth-quarter drive where he slipped. He looks like he has a bright future on this team, but Saturday’s game was not a good one for him

item.title: 3 quick takeaways from Badgers win over Rutgers: The Ryan Hopkins era is here
item.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 07: Ryan Hopkins #10 of the Wisconsin Badgers takes off running in the second quarter against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Camp Randall Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers blew out the Rutgers Scarlet Knights 31-10 on Saturday, earning bowl eligibility for the first time in three years as they improved to 6-2 on the season. True freshman Ryan Hopkins got his first career start, while the Badgers had another offensive line change. Still, they got out ahead early and finished the game strong en route to a blowout. Here are three quick takeaways from Wisconsin’s win over Rutgers. Hopkins has his moments For one of the first times this season, we saw the Badgers passing attack see some life. Yes, it was against a poor Rutgers team that didn’t have much pressure, but Hopkins looked fairly confident in the pocket and the Badgers let him rip. Hopkins made a number of good plays, as well as a few he would want back that didn’t end up hurting the Badgers. But he looked the part as a true freshman. He was very efficient throwing the ball, looked to target all parts of the field, and made throws that Colton Joseph hadn’t made. Wisconsin now gets a trial period with Hopkins over the next three games to assess where he’s at ahead of the 2027 season. But it was a very positive look in his first start. Pressuring the quarterback The Badgers came to play defensively, and a big part of it was getting after the quarterback. Wisconsin had five sacks, with Sebastian Cheeks, Nicolas Clayton, Charles Perkins, Nolan Vils, and Junior Poyser all getting sacks. They were able to pressure AJ Surace quite a bit, and stopping the run helped them get into third down situations, where they held Rutgers to 4 of 13 on third downs. It was a better day after Wisconsin couldn’t disrupt the quarterback against Iowa, with Hank Brown completing 20 of 24 passes for 222 yards. Good day for the boys up front. Bowl eligible It should be the expectation, but Wisconsin has returned to bowl eligibility after two disappointing years. It was a good bounce back for the Badgers, who were embarrassed last weekend, as they dominated Rutgers for much of this one. Now, the focus should be on Wisconsin winning at least two or the next three to take advantage of their favorable schedule. Going forward, the focus needs to be on Ryan Hopkins’s development and continued improvement of the offense, while Wisconsin’s defense remains to be aggressive. With how Wisconsin looked on Saturday, it feels like they must win that season-ender against Minnesota to cap off a successful season. But they had a strong performance Saturday and reached a key milestone.

item.description: MADISON, WI - NOVEMBER 07: Rutgers Scarlet Knights quarterback AJ Surace (10) throws a pass in a college football game between the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and the Wisconsin Badgers on November 7th, 2026 at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, WI. (Photo by Dan Sanger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rutgers football fell to Wisconsin 31 to 10 in a game where a three-point halftime deficit turned into a rout by the game’s end. In the final 30 minutes of play, the Scarlet Knights would be held scoreless while the Badgers found the momentum offensively to pull away. Rutgers would keep it close throughout the first half, as they only found themselves down by three at halftime. The Knights would force the Badgers to punt twice and would twice strand the Badgers on fourth down deep in their own territory twice, forcing them to take two field goals. Rutgers would keep pace by scoring a touchdown of their own, off of a 30-yard touchdown pass to freshman wide receiver Dyzier Carter, and by hitting a 45-yard field goal. The field goal was kicked by Jack Scullion, with starting kicker Dane Pizarro out due to injury. Wisconsin’s offense would start humming in the second half, with the Knights having no answer for it. The Badgers would kick a field goal on their first drive of the half to extend their lead before scoring two touchdowns on their next two drives. Rutgers’ defense would recover a fumble on Wisconsin’s fourth drive of the half, but their offense would be unable to score for the entire half as the Badgers would cruise to victory. The Knights’ defense continued the tradition of making backup freshman quarterbacks look like battle-tested veterans, as they allowed Ryan Hopkins to complete 18 out of 24 passes for 241 yards and three touchdowns. On the ground, Wisconsin ran the ball 29 times for 122 yards. On offense, the Knights struggled to keep their quarterback upright, as they surrendered five total sacks on the day and eight total tackles for loss. They also struggled to get the run going, totaling 94 yards on 36 carries, or 2.6 yards per carry. The one slight positive in this game is that AJ Surace looked more consistent in this game than in games past. He completed 14 out of 24 total passes for 161 yards, one touchdown, and no interceptions. This game was a step in the right direction for Surace, compared to his performance in games past. Rutgers will hope to get a few of their playmakers back healthy for next week, as they will return home to play the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Saturday, Nov. 14. Every loss is followed with a sarcastic rendition of ‘analytically, we actually won.’ Atkinson finally had a chance to clear the air before Cleveland’s rematch with the New York Knicks on Saturday night. “I answered the question of ‘you’re down 3-o, what hope do you guys have?’ and I wasn’t lying, but in no sense was it like ‘oh, we deserve to be winning’; there was zero thought of that,” said Atkinson. It’s not easy to give an optimistic spin when your team is trailing 0-3 in a series. Atkinson learned that the hard way. “I think when you look back on it and take the context of the question, I’m not sure that was taken into account, which was a little bit of a lesson for me,” said Atkinson. “I would just say, there was no coach more complimentary of the Knicks and honest about our performance and how they dominated us.” The Cavs were winning in some key expected margins during the series. Particularly in the first two games, where it felt like Cleveland was taking quality shots but just weren’t making them. All of that might help you sleep at night — but it doesn’t change the end result. Atkinson understands that. “As coaches, we have to check our process, like, are we getting the right shots?” said Atkinson. “But it kind of doesn’t matter, right? Because there’s more than that. There is the mental toughness and physical toughness. The flow of the game, how aggressive you are, there’s all these other intangibles that go in with that.”
